messages:
devon: Heads-up — since the EU wildcard cert rotation at 06:00 UTC we're seeing ~0.5% of requests get SSL handshake errors (502/526) at the ALB layer. Only affects traffic routed through the eu-west egress NAT pool.

sanjay: ugh. Is this happening for both v4 and v6? any pattern by load balancer or listener?

marta: i pulled a few ELB access logs — client_conn_error with 'TLS alert' and 'no shared cipher' shows up, but the backend app logs show no request at all. ALB returns before target group.

devon: only v4 so far, all on ALB listeners on port 443, listener rules unchanged. This started right after we applied the wildcard cert from the internal ACME pipeline to the ALB (replaced cert arn).

lena: could be clienthello SNI being stripped for keepalive connections through our NAT gateway. We had one NAT instance that kept long-lived outbound connections — if the ALB sees re-used client connections without SNI it will pick default cert which might mismatch.

ben: can we reproduce with openssl s_client? try sweeping a few client IPs that hit the problematic NAT. Also check ALB TLS policy and ALPN.

devon: trying openssl. here's an example:
openssl s_client -connect alb-eu-west-1-012345678.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com:443 -servername api.eu.redwood.local -alpn h2
returned: "CONNECTED(00000003)\n140735...: TLSv1.2 handshake failure (err code: 1)"

marta: also seeing `ClientHello` truncated in tcpdump from the NAT IP, length shows 0 or missing SNI extension. looks like some middlebox re-writing or a bug in client TLS stacks.

infra-bot: [alert] 1902345678 - automatic rollback prevented (no target group health issues)

sanjay: check ALB listener cert rotation overlap window — did we rotate with zero-downtime (attach new cert, keep old cert until validation) or swap ARNs immediately? if old cert removed early and a keepalive hits during swap, you could get default cert served (or handshake failure).

devon: rotation was attach-new then detach-old after 5 mins. But logs show some connections from the same source IP reusing a TCP connection that predates the attach — ALB apparently renegotiates and expects SNI. If SNI is missing handshake fails.

lena: Another angle: ingress controller annotation for ALB target groups — do we have proxy-protocol enabled? If proxy header is malformed for TLS listeners, ALB might abort before SNI parse. Show me ingress annotation.

devon: our ingress has: `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "443"`, `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/target-type: instance`, `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-policy: ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS-1-2-2017-01`

ben: hmm policy is fine. Can you capture `openssl s_client -msg -state` output and tcpdump side-by-side for a failing request? Also check NAT gateway logs / flow logs — maybe there was a kernel-level packet coalescing bug that stripped SNI bytes.

marta: i grabbed a failing pcap: clienthello only 34 bytes and no extensions. It looks like upstream client restarted with 0-RTT or a buggy TLS stack. But it's concentrated to an autoscaled customer IP range that uses an old proxy.

devon: mitigation: added listener rule fallback to return `403` with `x-ssl-error` header for requests that fail early, and re-attached old cert for another hour to soak. So far percentages dropped to ~0.05%.

lena: long term: we should enable ALB TLS policy that tolerates missing SNI? I don't think ALB supports that. Better: enable per-listener certificate fallback ordering and increase rotation overlap to 24h for EU region given known legacy proxies. Also add NAT pool refresh so ephemeral connections don't sticky to NAT instances across cert rotations.

sanjay: Agreed. Action items: 1) extend rotation overlap window for all wildcard certs in EU to 24h (platform config), 2) add NAT pool churn step to rotation runbook, 3) instrument `client_hello_size` metric at ingress/ALB (maybe via packet mirroring) and alert >0.1%.

ben: I'll open infra ticket and tag security for certificate policy change. devon, update the incident doc with the mitigation and pcap link.

devon: done — added notes + pcap to the incident binder. ping me if you want to replay captures or repro. :thumbsup:

marta: FYI we also saw a small cluster of mTLS services (internal only) that failed because our sidecars expect SNI to map client cert to SAN, so extended overlap helps there too.

infra-bot: [incident-id: eu-alb-clienthello-1902345678] severity: low -> auto-closed after mitigation window

sanjay: thanks team — leaving this thread open for postmortem comments.
